Red Cliff is the first part of John Woo's epic war film about the Battle of Red Cliffs, fought at the close of China's Han dynasty, just before the Three Kingdoms era. Running 146 minutes, it premiered in Beijing in July 2008, with the second part following in January 2009; outside Asia the two were cut into a single film of 148 minutes. It was Woo's first Chinese-language feature since Hard Boiled. Tony Leung stars as the southern commander Zhou Yu, with Takeshi Kaneshiro as the strategist Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fengyi as the warlord Cao Cao, Chang Chen as Sun Quan, Zhao Wei as his sister Lady Sun, Hu Jun as Zhao Yun, You Yong as Liu Bei and Lin Chi-ling as Zhou Yu's wife Xiaoqiao. Woo said the story is only about half based on history.

In 208 AD Cao Cao, who controls the puppet Emperor Xian, wins the reluctant emperor's approval for a campaign against the southern warlords Liu Bei and Sun Quan, branding them rebels. His vast army quickly overruns Jing Province and catches Liu Bei's forces at Changban, where the sworn brothers Guan Yu and Zhang Fei shield the fleeing civilians and Zhao Yun battles through the enemy, managing to rescue only Liu Bei's infant son.

Liu Bei's adviser Zhuge Liang then travels to Jiangdong to seek an alliance with Sun Quan, who is torn between surrender and war. Won over by Zhuge Liang's arguments and a tiger hunt with Zhou Yu and Lady Sun, Sun Quan chooses to fight. Two naval officers from Jing Province, Cai Mao and Zhang Yun, defect to Cao Cao, who gives them command of his enormous fleet. As Cao Cao's forces advance on the allied base at Red Cliff by land and river, Lady Sun lures his vanguard into the allies' Eight Trigrams formation, where it is destroyed in a fierce battle. Unshaken, Cao Cao camps his main army across the river from Red Cliff. While the allies celebrate, Lady Sun slips away to spy on the enemy camp, sending reports to Zhuge Liang by carrier pigeon, setting the stage for the decisive battle of the second part.

As Cao Cao's vast army and fleet camp across the river from Red Cliff, Lady Sun Shangxiang, sister of the warlord Sun Quan, infiltrates the enemy camp and sends details to the strategist Zhuge Liang by carrier pigeon. When typhoid strikes his troops, Cao Cao sends the corpses on rafts to spread the plague to his enemies, and a disheartened Liu Bei withdraws, apparently breaking the alliance, while Zhuge Liang stays to help Sun Quan. Zhou Yu and Zhuge Liang wager their lives on rival tasks: eliminating Cao Cao's naval commanders Cai Mao and Zhang Yun, and obtaining 100,000 arrows. Zhuge Liang sends straw-covered boats to draw enemy fire and collects the arrows, while Zhou Yu deceives the envoy Jiang Gan, and together the ruses lead Cao Cao to execute his two admirals. Predicting that the winds will turn to blow from the southeast, the allies plan a fire attack on Cao Cao's interlocked fleet, as Zhou Yu's wife Xiaoqiao goes alone to Cao Cao's camp and stalls him with an elaborate tea ceremony. When the wind rises at night, burning boats ram the enemy ships while Liu Bei's forces, whose departure was a ruse, strike on land. By dawn the fleet is destroyed, and after a costly assault on Cao Cao's main camp, the allies gain the upper hand but spare his life.

Red Cliff Part II was released in China on 7 January 2009, and the 142-minute film completed a two-part version running nearly five hours, while Western audiences first saw a single abridged 148-minute cut in 2009. It was shot in Beijing and Hebei. The Hollywood Reporter praised Woo's ordering of the narrative and kinetic action, which propel the film to a thundering climax, and Variety, calling the second half heavier on action yet rich in human interest, judged the two-part version one of the great Chinese costume epics of all time.

The film opens with Fidel Castro publicly reading, in October 1965, the farewell letter in which Che renounces his Cuban posts and citizenship after vanishing from public life. A year later Guevara, disguised as an older Uruguayan official named Ramón, travels with forged papers to La Paz and on into the mountains to join a small band of Cuban veterans and Bolivian recruits. Training and arms deliveries mark the early days, but the Bolivian Communist Party under Mario Monje refuses to back armed struggle, local peasants remain wary or hostile, food runs short and quarrels flare between Cubans and Bolivians. Deserters lead the army to the rebels' base camp, exposing the foreign identity of the group, while President René Barrientos accepts American help and U.S. advisers begin training Bolivian Rangers to hunt them down.

The journalist Régis Debray and the Argentine Ciro Bustos are arrested after leaving the camp, a rear guard that includes the agent Tania is wiped out in an ambush at a river crossing, and Guevara, increasingly crippled by asthma, leads a dwindling column through the forest. Wounded and captured in a firefight near La Higuera, he is held in the village school and executed on 9 October 1967.
